## Graphics delivery priorities — current acceptance gates

This is the current work order, not a claim that the scene is close to AAA.
Dated sections below retain evidence and superseded experiments.

1. [ ] **Ground materials:** Grass004 is selected by matched native views;
   finish cliff material/landform, motion, transfer, mips and compression.
2. [ ] **Grounded lighting:** separate direct/neutral/contact-AO comparisons;
   preserve skin color, sunlight, cutout foliage and water without halos.
3. [ ] **A composed compact island:** improve landform, worn paths, shoreline,
   lodge/workshop/bank setting, props and furnished interiors. One arena only.
4. [ ] **Fuller living vegetation:** actual choppable resource trees throughout
   the island; coherent species/scale, correct grass contact, denser meadow and
   shrubs where appropriate. No decorative tree replacement of game resources.
5. [ ] **Characters and equipment:** finish in-scene materials, animation,
   clipping/fit and all item bindings; final directional/grip review stays open.
6. [ ] **Atmosphere and motion:** polish sky, water, shadows, wind, camera cuts,
   combat/gathering movement, soundscape and SFX as a coherent experience.
7. [ ] **Measured quality at scale:** agreed hardware/scene budgets, actual GPU
   and presented-frame evidence, cold loading, multi-agent motion and thermal
   soak. Fixed-resolution screenshots and passing CPU tests are not this gate.
8. [ ] **Integrated launch:** agent preparation/combat/resource lifetimes,
   streaming/video/audio, reconnect/recovery and SOL-only real-money safety.
   Keep the outstanding cow/dagger failures visible until genuinely fixed.

## Active goal — Hyperia AAA-quality world and experience

Created 2026-09-10 at the user's explicit request. Build on and perfect the
existing game; do not restart the renderer, replace approved anatomy, or discard
working gameplay/optimization systems. This goal spans the existing milestones;
it does not redefine their payment terms or call the current diagnostics an MVP.

**Outcome:** one cohesive, beautiful, responsive, fully playable compact agent
island with complete usable assets and a reliable preparation → duel → recovery
and spectator/stream experience. Replace the large island; a separate legacy-world
preset is not required. “AAA” is
the visual and experiential ambition; it is not an objective certification or a
substitute for the acceptance evidence below.

### Delivery sequence and acceptance

- [ ] **G01 — Visual standard and performance baseline.** Record reference shots
  and a consistent art/material/scale guide using the current approved body and
  asset direction. Define target hardware, browser, actual drawing-buffer
  resolution, streaming output, representative actor counts and stress cases.
  Record cold/warm load, CPU/GPU frame distributions, stalls, memory, draw calls,
  triangle/texture budgets and long-run drift. Target smooth 60 fps on the
  designated desktop/streaming tier; define exact per-tier pass thresholds from
  measured baselines before accepting content. Do not silently change resolution,
  scene population, quality tier or the target device to manufacture a pass.
- [ ] **G02 — Avatar and equipped-lighting correctness.** Fix the current cyan
  night-light cast and separate neutral armor-reflection setup. Skin, eyes,
  metal, cloth and leather must read coherently in the same scene at noon,
  dusk and night, equipped and unequipped. Preserve source texture/color-space
  correctness, transmission and approved anatomy. Verify close front/side/rear
  views plus movement; do not repaint skin or boost emissive/exposure to conceal
  a lighting defect. A studio PMREM is a diagnostic, not a final outdoor solution.
- [ ] **G03 — Complete asset library and actual game bindings.** Finish every
  required avatar, armor, shield, weapon, bow, projectile, tool and supporting
  item family. Cover all 260 canonical item IDs with exact mappings; metal tiers
  reuse geometry and vary controlled material colors. Verify portable exports,
  textures, rigging, deformation, equipping/removal, armor coverage, layered
  clothing/shorts replacement, socket directions, projectiles and tool use.
  Preserve sources and provisional grip checkpoints. Final shared/distinct grip
  polish stays last, followed by all affected animation/attachment regressions.
- [ ] **G04 — Compact playable island vertical slice.** First complete a coherent
  arena-to-bank/preparation area with representative terrain, shoreline, water,
  path, workstation, vegetation and equipped actors. Then extend that same
  standard to the whole compact island. Place every required gathering,
  banking, crafting, cooking, training and loadout service within verified short
  routes; preserve canonical resource identities, not the old large-world preset.
  Check nav/collision, slopes, diagonal routes, spawns, replenishment, interaction
  reach, line of sight and repeated agent travel—not just map composition.
- [ ] **G05 — Terrain, shoreline, water and set dressing.** Finish terrain
  silhouettes, ground-material blending, shoreline transitions, water, paths,
  arena architecture, banks/buildings/workstations, rocks and props. Use
  consistent world units, texel density, pivots, contact and readable landmarks.
  Remove floating/intersecting props, visible seams and mismatched scales;
  include collision and interaction bounds in placement/export validation.
- [ ] **G06 — Trees, foliage and grass.** Build a cohesive vegetation palette
  with intentional density, wind, ground contact, harvesting feedback, readable
  paths and stable silhouettes. Reuse instancing, chunking, culling and existing
  LOD/impostor systems. Verify transition stability, alpha/overdraw, shadows,
  close/distant views, streaming/pop-in and crowded agent/resource areas.
- [ ] **G07 — Unified renderer polish.** Tune outdoor environment lighting,
  day/night palette and transitions, tone mapping, exposure, sun/moon, shadows,
  contact, fog, water and restrained effects as one system. Establish shadow
  distance/resolution/cascade budgets; remove acne, detached shadows, flicker,
  missing receivers and unexpected color shifts. Repeated renders, precompile,
  loads and disposals must remain free of relevant GPU validation failures.
- [ ] **G08 — Motion and experience polish.** Verify full-kit idle/walk/run,
  smooth turns and diagonals, combat-style changes, ranged movement, spells,
  gathering/crafting, hits/death and transitions without clipping, foot sliding
  or broken attachments. Finish readable effects, feedback, cameras and UI;
  spectators must understand both agent preparation and duels. Check stream
  composition, loading/reconnect states and audiovisual synchronization.
- [ ] **G09 — Scale and lifecycle optimization.** Enforce per-family LOD,
  geometry/material/texture and animation budgets in actual populated gameplay.
  Reuse existing culling, instancing, chunk streaming, caches, workers and bounded
  updates. Verify independent actor state, repeated equipment switching,
  environment/shadow changes and resource disposal; collect long-duration
  frame/memory trends and load/reconnect/restart evidence. Triangle reductions
  or short stationary frame samples alone do not satisfy this gate.
- [ ] **G10 — Integrated acceptance and handoff.** Run the completed island and
  assets through actual agent preparation/banking/crafting, dynamic duels,
  recovery, spectator cameras and streaming. Preserve authoritative timing and
  Solana-only betting behavior. Exercise multiple agents, long/short fights,
  failures/restarts and sustained operation. Produce a reviewable walkthrough,
  matched visual evidence and measured performance report. No unresolved
  critical visual/gameplay/reliability defects, missing required asset bindings
  or untested target-tier performance may be relabeled “production ready.”

## Delivery milestones

These milestones are the contract and payment reporting view over the detailed launch gates below. A milestone is complete only when its acceptance evidence is recorded in this checklist; completing a milestone never waives an unresolved P0/P1 task that falls within it.

### Milestone 1 — End-to-end functional beta

- [~] Deliver one repeatable autonomous loop in which agents prepare through authoritative gameplay, use banking and frozen duel loadouts, enter scheduled dynamic combat, stream the preparation/fight/result sequence, and drive the matching Hyperbet market lifecycle. Native-SOL order, settlement, cancellation, and refund behavior must pass on the approved local-validator or non-production test rail with no manual state repair.
- Acceptance evidence: recorded end-to-end demonstration; focused and broad automated gates; exact gameplay/market identity and custody reconciliation; documented multi-cycle reliability run; every remaining limitation explicitly listed rather than hidden behind diagnostic fixtures.

### Milestone 2 — Launch candidate: UI, 3D, UX, and performance

- [~] Deliver the polished public experience across desktop and mobile: production-quality Hyperbet UI, duel/preparation presentation, approved avatar/equipment assets, animation/movement/rotation/camera/effects/audio, broadcast overlays and transitions, accessible degraded/reconnect/transaction states, and smooth client/server/render/stream behavior.
- Acceptance evidence: agreed visual and interaction matrix; responsive/accessibility review; reproducible performance capture on agreed hardware; target-loss, stream-loss, RPC, reconnect, and restart fault injection; agreed extended soak; final manual product approval with no developer explanation required.

### Milestone 3 — Production launch readiness and handoff

- [ ] Deliver the SOL-only production system with verified program identities and roles, approved configuration and economics, security/release gates, secrets and access controls, monitoring/alerts, backup/rollback/cancellation/stream-failover runbooks, clean staging rehearsal, launch evidence package, operational documentation, and knowledge-transfer handoff.
- Acceptance evidence: every engineering launch blocker closed; production-shaped staging rehearsal passes using the release commands and manifests; launch-day rehearsal and operator handoff complete; public real-value wagering remains fail-closed until every client-controlled approval below is supplied.

Client-controlled dependencies do not become hidden engineering acceptance criteria: qualified legal/compliance and jurisdictional approval; approved fees, limits, treasury and market rules; production Solana program deployment authority and addresses; production RPC/streaming credentials and infrastructure; approved final assets, target hardware, and product sign-off. Engineering can be accepted as production-ready while activation remains disabled pending those inputs.

## Status and severity

- `[x]` Verified complete on the current branch.
- `[~]` Implemented or actively being validated; not yet a launch pass.
- `[ ]` Not complete.
- `P0` blocks launch or can cause incorrect gameplay, settlement, loss of funds, a stuck market, or a broken stream.
- `P1` required for a polished public experience.
- `P2` valuable follow-up that is not required for the first safe launch.

Maker-signed cancel and reclaim close the `Order` PDA to the maker; a separate maker-authorized `close_filled_order` instruction closes only an inactive, fully filled, unlinked, non-continuation Order and cannot move collateral, vault funds, or shared `PriceLevel` rent. The UI derives actual Order lamports from the live account, revalidates ownership/lifecycle/links/rent immediately before signature, and shows exact returned collateral, Order rent, and gross wallet credit. The keeper records an exact `FILLED_ORDER_CLOSED` lifecycle fact with no amount fields, and reconciliation proves this account-rent event cannot change collateral, fee, reward, payout, or refund totals.
- Shared `PriceLevel` rent custody is implemented with immutable first-payer attribution. Every initialization records the actual payer before matching; reuse validates but never overwrites the recipient; immediate empty closure occurs only when the current signer is that recipient; otherwise `close_empty_price_level` accepts any signer but Anchor constrains the close destination to the recorded wallet and rejects nonempty state. Generated clients and every downstream IDL include the enlarged 100-byte account and cleanup instruction. Keeper parsing binds the exact four-account graph, recipient, submitter signature, PDA, side/price, and zero inner transfers, then stores a no-amount `PRICE_LEVEL_CLOSED` fact that cannot alter betting reconciliation. Fresh-validator tests prove initialization, multi-maker reuse, partial/full fill, middle/head/tail cancel, terminal reclaim attribution, unrelated dormant-level IOC reuse, wrong-recipient/nonempty rejection, exact recipient and submitter wallet deltas, concurrent cleanup with exactly one success, account closure, and replay rejection. Cleanup submitter/automation/fee-threshold/product disclosure policy remains intentionally unapproved.
- Execution-fee custody is now terminal-outcome safe without changing the existing fee rates or split. Each market snapshots immutable treasury and market-maker recipients; each payer's separately rounded fee components remain in the canonical market vault and are tracked on both `MarketState` and `UserBalance`. A cancelled/no-contest claim returns matched collateral plus that payer's exact two fee components and drains only their attribution. A resolved market permits one exact, permissionless, destination-constrained release to the snapshotted recipients; open, locked, cancelled, redirected, empty, and replay attempts reject. The UI quotes these execution fees as refundable on cancellation, the finalized keeper path requires exact escrow/claim/release events and transfers, cancellation settlement attributes each fee to its originating order, and keeper automation releases resolved fees after canonical settlement. This closes protocol-controlled cancellation fee loss; network fees remain outside Hyperbet control.

## SOL-only v1 architecture and implementation order

The only supported v1 path is:

`Hyperia duel authority and schema-v3 feed -> Solana keeper/control plane -> fight_oracle -> duel_market CLOB -> Solana betting app`

The renderer/capture/delivery path consumes the same authoritative duel identity and phase clock; it must not invent a separate matchup, timer, result, or market state. No EVM, BSC, Base, AVAX/Avalanche, perps, model market, AMM, GOLD token, or token-conversion path is part of v1. A hidden route or disabled selector is not sufficient: excluded code must be absent from the production bundle, runtime dependency graph, deploy manifests, launch CI, and operator runbooks.

## P0 — Hyperbet lifecycle and fund safety

Launch-scope decision on 2026-08-03: v1 is a single-chain SOL product. AVAX/Avalanche, BSC/BNB, Base/ETH, and every other chain are out of scope and must be removed from the public/runtime/deployment launch surface. The current Solana registry addresses are not reusable; SOL-first requires a clean audited program deployment.

- [x] Introduce an explicit feed outcome for `win` and `draw` in Hyperia schema v3.
- [x] Route a draw through Hyperia betting/oracle cancellation paths instead of winner settlement.
- [x] Add explicit `cancelled`/no-contest terminal semantics to the external feed, including a reason, terminal timestamp, immediate SSE broadcast, and reconnect replay retention.
- [x] Update every Hyperbet feed parser and public stream state to preserve `outcome` and `cancellationReason`.
- [x] Update every Hyperbet game client to treat `draw` and `cancelled` as terminal refund events.

## P0 — Native-token-only markets, fee fairness, and GOLD removal

Launch policy: Hyperbet v1 accepts only native SOL on Solana. Every non-Solana chain is removed from the v1 product, bundle, runtime, deployment, and public documentation. There is no GOLD token, GOLD conversion, GOLD balance/staking boost, or six-decimal GOLD accounting in the launch product. The visual color name “gold” and a non-token loyalty tier named “Gold” may remain only if they cannot be mistaken for an asset; all token semantics must be removed.

Audit snapshot on 2026-08-03: the CLOB contracts/program already custody native value (`msg.value` on EVM and lamports/system transfers on Solana), but 260 source files and 2,094 source lines match actionable GOLD-token/product identifiers, 77 files contain the standalone word `GOLD`, and 121 tracked paths contain `gold`. The current UI, APIs, database, SDKs, registry, environment variables, deployment artifacts, tests, scripts, and disabled perps/AMM surfaces are not yet native-token clean. After the SOL-only decision, a raw scan of the Solana package plus shared UI/registry/SDK/deployments and root scripts still found `gold`/`GOLD` in 183 files and 1,689 lines, with 30 files containing standalone `GOLD` and 37 in-scope paths containing `gold`; 117 of the matching files are under `packages/hyperbet-solana`. These raw counts include false positives such as visual colors and must be classified, but they show that focusing on Solana does not make the token migration small.

Current external benchmark: [Polymarket's official fee documentation](https://docs.polymarket.com/trading/fees) uses category-dependent match-time taker fees, charges makers zero, and directs part of fees to liquidity incentives. [Kalshi's July 2026 official fee schedule](https://kalshi.com/docs/kalshi-fee-schedule.pdf) uses price-sensitive trading fees and states that simple event-contract settlement has no fee. These benchmarks support removing Hyperbet's separate winnings fee; the recommended 100 bps launch rate still requires Hyperbet-specific sensitivity and retention evidence.

Current versus recommended fee burden for a taker who buys one share and wins, normalized to a native payout of `1` (network gas excluded):

| Entry price | Current: 2% entry + 2% winning share | Current fee as % of entry | Recommended: 1% entry only |
| ----------- | ------------------------------------ | ------------------------- | -------------------------- |
| `0.10`      | `0.022`                              | `22.0%`                   | `0.001`                    |
| `0.50`      | `0.030`                              | `6.0%`                    | `0.005`                    |
| `0.90`      | `0.038`                              | `4.22%`                   | `0.009`                    |

The current winnings fee is especially punitive to successful long-shot bets and is charged in addition to an already-paid execution fee. A losing taker still pays the 2% execution fee today.

At the recommended 100 bps / 80:20 split, each `$1,000,000` of USD-equivalent taker collateral on resolved markets yields `$10,000` gross protocol fees: `$8,000` treasury revenue and `$2,000` liquidity incentives. The first-pass monthly break-even formula is `net operating cost / 0.008`; cancelled/refunded volume does not count as revenue. This is a planning formula, not proof of profitability.

Fee sensitivity per `$1,000,000` of resolved taker collateral, assuming the same 80:20 treasury/liquidity split:

| Taker fee | Gross fees | Treasury contribution before operating costs | Monthly break-even volume    |
| --------- | ---------- | -------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------- |
| `50 bps`  | `$5,000`   | `$4,000`                                     | `net operating cost / 0.004` |
| `75 bps`  | `$7,500`   | `$6,000`                                     | `net operating cost / 0.006` |
| `100 bps` | `$10,000`  | `$8,000`                                     | `net operating cost / 0.008` |

The launcher parses both exact `packageManager` declarations, requires the orchestrator process itself to be Hyperia's exact runtime, resolves Hyperbet's exact runtime separately only when that workspace is in scope, routes every child to the correct verified executable, exposes a read-only `--check-runtimes` preflight, and rejects a mismatched global runtime before any build, database, browser, stream, keeper, or market process. Live-audit snapshot on 2026-08-03: a two-agent local stress run reached real scheduler-controlled fights, so the rendering path is no longer hypothetical, but it failed the launch-quality bar. On a 600-frame Chromium spectator sample at 1280×720, frame time was p50 9.1 ms, p95 41.1 ms, p99 127.7 ms, and max 243.4 ms; 39/600 frames exceeded 33 ms and 22/600 exceeded 50 ms. This local headless sample is diagnostic evidence, not a production benchmark. Server-side, terrain updates repeatedly consumed 100–1,900 ms, event-loop blocks exceeded two seconds, missed ticks rose to 83, mob population grew from 164 to 1,031 by shutdown during the short run, and the memory monitor reported sustained heap growth around 68 MB/min. Multiple cycles aborted for `no_combat_activity`, agent spacing repeatedly became invalid, and the stream presented colliding nameplates/health bars, visually overlapping fighters, weak camera composition, and missing assets/collision.

## P0 — Legal, compliance, responsible wagering, and market integrity

This checklist is an engineering control, not legal advice. Native-token wagering must not open to the public until qualified counsel signs off on the exact product, entity, jurisdictions, contracts, custody/flow of funds, marketing, and operating model. The regulatory environment is active: the [CFTC's June 2026 proposed event-contract framework](https://www.cftc.gov/PressRoom/PressReleases/9249-26) expressly discusses gaming and activities unlawful under federal or state law; [FinCEN guidance](https://www.fincen.gov/resources/statutes-regulations/guidance/application-fincens-regulations-persons-administering) addresses when accepting/transmitting convertible virtual currency can be money transmission; and [OFAC guidance](https://ofac.treasury.gov/system/files/126/virtual_currency_guidance_brochure.pdf) states that sanctions obligations apply to virtual-currency transactions.

Repository audit snapshot on 2026-08-03: source-only runtime searches found no implemented KYC, AML, sanctions screening, geofencing, age verification, source-of-funds, self-exclusion, or responsible-wagering enforcement. The current CLOB source does prevent a directly matching wallet from trading against itself, and the repository includes adversarial wash/sybil/spoofing simulations, but those simulations are not connected production surveillance and same-wallet prevention does not stop coordinated or multi-wallet abuse.

- [ ] Obtain written counsel sign-off for every served jurisdiction and chain, including event-contract/gaming/gambling, derivatives, money-transmission, consumer-protection, privacy, tax/reporting, and licensing analysis; record prohibited jurisdictions and product constraints.
- [~] Keep real-value betting disabled by default until the legal launch gate is signed; test geofencing and fail closed when location or eligibility cannot be established. The active SOL app now defaults transaction authority off, and a source-level policy keeps every mainnet/mainnet-beta build spectator-only even when a deployment attempts `VITE_TRANSACTIONS_ENABLED=true`; only localnet/devnet/testnet can opt into signing for valueless verification. The production Pages workflow now emits an explicit read-only build, the environment audit rejects any transaction-enabled production or preview artifact, and the production keeper audit fails before Railway mutation. Independently, the duel bot refuses mainnet market creation before reading any signer configuration, with no environment escape hatch. A clean frozen-lock snapshot passes strict app/keeper TypeScript, 65/65 app tests and 188/188 shared-UI tests, 286/286 keeper launch tests including cross-repository process-kill recovery, and 5/5 deployment-environment tests. A hostile mainnet build plus headless artifact check proves `data-market-can-place-bet=false`, a `Live match details` read-only rail, spectator-only copy, and zero Place Bet or wallet-connect controls. This closes the default-disable/bypass boundary only. Counsel sign-off, approved jurisdiction rules, geolocation/eligibility/KYC enforcement, on-chain or otherwise non-bypassable user controls, and adversarial staging remain open; mainnet value must stay disabled until all are implemented and approved.
- [ ] Implement the counsel-approved age, identity/KYC, AML, sanctions/wallet screening, source-of-funds, transaction-monitoring, recordkeeping, escalation, and reporting controls before accepting native tokens.
- [ ] Publish versioned market rules that define participants, authoritative data source, opening/lock timing, win/draw/no-contest conditions, interruption/replay policy, dispute process, fee math, gas treatment, cancellation refunds, claim deadlines, and governing terms before a wallet signs.
- [ ] Add responsible-wagering controls appropriate to the approved jurisdictions: configurable deposit/stake/loss/time limits, cooling-off and self-exclusion, clear risk disclosures, no misleading “guaranteed profit” language, and support/escalation procedures.
- [ ] Establish an operator/employee/contractor/agent-owner trading policy. People or systems with non-public duel state, agent-control access, oracle keys, scheduler authority, market-maker control, or settlement authority must be barred or tightly controlled and monitored from trading affected markets.
- [ ] Separate duties and credentials across game/scheduler operations, reporter, challenger, finalizer, pauser, market operator, market maker, treasury, and admin; no single actor should be able to influence a duel, settle it, and profit from the same market without independent detection and approval.
- [ ] Add market-surveillance rules and alerts for wash/self trading, collusion, suspicious related wallets, oracle/stream timing abuse, last-second information advantage, price manipulation, bot abuse, referral farming, multi-account evasion, and abnormal win rates.
- [ ] Treat contract-level same-wallet self-trade prevention as one narrow control, not a complete market-integrity system. ## Evidence log

- 2026-08-28 — Latest generic player-health snapshot recovery across a same-live-world PostgreSQL outage: a fail-before ordering regression reproduced the defect with one failure among three assertions—the generic save buffer was deleted before database acknowledgement, so damage, healing, regeneration, or respawn state could be lost and an older in-flight snapshot could later overwrite a newer pool. `DatabaseSystem.savePlayer` now retains a coalesced per-player/per-field latest snapshot until acknowledgement, assigns monotonic field revisions, serializes generic and awaited row writes, retries the one bounded global batch once per second, and throttles non-sensitive failure logs. A newer awaited save acknowledges only overlapping older fields; distinct failed fields remain queued. Graceful shutdown makes three bounded drain attempts before repositories reject work. Seven ordering regressions pass, including transient shutdown retry and stale-overwrite prevention. The production-built live-world gate applies all 93 migrations, pauses PostgreSQL with `6/10` already in flight, authors a newer `5/10` pool through healing plus damage during the outage, restores PostgreSQL, and proves durable convergence to exactly `5/10` with zero buffered players or revision maps; two consecutive final runs pass and remove their owned containers. All nine real PostgreSQL `DatabaseSystem` integration files pass 17/17; the independent food `SIGKILL`/outage/replacement gate remains exact; complete server coverage passes 2,780 with 124 intentional skips and complete shared coverage passes 5,793 with 23 intentional skips. Strict server/shared TypeScript, changed-surface zero-warning lint, formatting, whitespace, and the production server/worker build (`6be1e42db1d3`) pass. Evidence is `artifacts/player-health-live-world-outage-20260828/evidence.json`, SHA-256 `7be418dae3320356e86d44ef13a0487a1261d97510a8759eff73a36171b03ed1`. This closes positive-health generic latest-snapshot recovery in one continuously running world—not process loss while PostgreSQL is unavailable, lethal-zero/death-custody outage semantics, production-population throughput/contention, multi-host database availability, production-equivalent infrastructure, or the ten-hour combined loop. No browser, avatar/equipment/model, wallet, signature, SOL transfer, public endpoint, deployment, commit, push, or real value was touched.

- 2026-08-28 — Same-live-world ordinary-food database-outage and autosave-race recovery: fail-before component tests showed that a pre-commit ambiguous custody response retained no exact live operation identity, while a post-commit completion failure could hold the optimistic heal indefinitely. ## Current SOL program, economics, and staged-proof closeout

- [x] The shipping Anchor workspace contains exactly `fight_oracle` and
      `duel_market`; build, client generation, deployment, initialization, and
      verification commands no longer fan out into retired programs or chains.
- [x] Fresh complete IDLs are synchronized byte-for-byte across the Anchor
      target, SOL app, SOL keeper, and shared UI. The duel-market normalized ABI is
      locked by an exact compatibility gate.
- [x] SOL launch initialization and verification fail closed on invalid roles,
      frozen configuration drift, program identity drift, fee drift, cluster
      genesis-hash drift, upgradeable-loader/ProgramData linkage drift, and
      deployed-binary hash drift. Remote verification requires every authority and
      role explicitly, requires both reproducible local SBF binaries, and never
      records the RPC endpoint or credentials in its evidence artifact.
- [x] Execution fees remain in the canonical native-SOL vault with exact payer
      attribution until terminal outcome. Cancelled, drawn, and no-contest markets
      refund each payer's execution-fee escrow with collateral; resolved markets
      release the snapshotted treasury and market-maker fee fields exactly once.
      Post-only makers remain free, takers pay only on executed quantity, and the
      compatible program enforces bounded fee values without requiring a new ABI.
- [~] Production economics remain deliberately unapproved. The keeper's local and
  non-mainnet diagnostic defaults are 100 bps treasury execution fee, 100 bps
  market-maker execution fee, and 200 bps winnings fee; they are test parameters,
  not a launch decision. Mainnet refuses to start without the exact approval flag
  and all three explicitly configured values. Current launch guardrails require
  at least 1 treasury execution-fee bps, cap combined execution fees at 500 bps,
  and cap winnings fees at 500 bps; product, finance, compliance, and engineering
  must approve a fair/profitable triplet and immutable recipients before staging.
- [x] The manual staged proof is devnet/testnet only, requires an exact explicit
      write confirmation, creates a fresh duel and trader identity, verifies three
      separated roles, matches opposing native-SOL orders, cancels the duel, claims
      both refunds, checks closed/zeroed balances, and requires the vault to return
      exactly to baseline.
- [x] The same staged driver now has a resolved-winner scenario with a distinct
      finalizer, immutable lock transition, proposal/dispute-window/finalization,
      exact winner fee routing, successful zero-payout loser cleanup, closed balance
      PDAs, and exact terminal vault conservation. The compatible on-chain `claim`
      instruction now permits that loser cleanup without changing the ABI.
- [x] CI and deployment command surfaces are SOL-only. Deployment workflows are
      manual, the staged proof cannot select mainnet, the obsolete mixed-chain soak
      and proof drivers are removed, and policy gates prevent those paths from
      returning.
- [x] Run the fresh-validator SBF/Anchor integration lane with the pinned
      compiler and an actual upgradeable-loader authority. The exact recommended
      Anchor 0.32.1, Solana/Agave 2.3.0, and platform-tools v1.48 toolchain built
      both deployable programs twice with byte-identical hashes, and the complete

      authority and policy checks prevent immutable preload or toolchain drift.

      manual, protected-environment SOL-only devnet/testnet gate. It rebuilds both
      launch programs, checks ABI compatibility, then verifies cluster identity,
      program bytes, loader ownership, ProgramData links, deployment slots, upgrade
